questions.q: What are the five core functions of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, in order?
options: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover
Plan, Build, Test, Deploy, Monitor
Prevent, Detect, Encrypt, Audit, Certify
Scope, Assess, Patch, Report, Close
questions.explain: NIST organizes cybersecurity activity into these five functions, which map onto ideas like layered defense (Protect) and incident response (Respond).

questions.q: Which NIST function does the layered defense model from the earlier lesson map onto most directly?
options: Protect
Identify
Detect
Recover
questions.explain: Protect covers the safeguards an organization puts in place, which is exactly what the perimeter/network/endpoint/access layers are.

questions.q: What does ISO 27001 actually specify requirements for?
options: An Information Security Management System (ISMS) — the ongoing, organization-wide process of managing security risk
A specific brand of firewall every certified company must use
A one-time checklist with no ongoing process
A government-mandated password length for all employees
questions.explain: ISO 27001 is a standard for building and running an ISMS, not a single technical setting or one-time checklist.

questions.q: What does it mean for an organization to be "certified" against ISO 27001?
options: An outside auditor reviewed the organization's ISMS and confirmed it meets the standard's requirements
The organization self-declared compliance with no outside review
The organization purchased a specific software license
The organization passed a government background check
questions.explain: Certification involves an independent auditor confirming the ISMS meets ISO 27001's requirements, producing a certificate the organization can show others.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three real reasons organizations pursue compliance, according to this lesson?
options: Guaranteeing the organization will never experience a breach
Legal requirement in regulated industries
Customer trust, as independent proof of security practices
Contractual obligation required by business partners or customers
questions.explain: Compliance reduces risk and formalizes good practice, but no framework or certification guarantees a breach will never happen.
